title: Early Emission Kernel Coordinator — Model Admission & Rollback Notes
content:
Purpose

Notes exploring a lightweight coordinator that drives early-emission (emit candidate tokens before full KV fetch) across model onboarding, plus acceptance/rollback contracts and instrumentation requirements. The aim is to enable modest latency wins on long-tail low-latency requests while bounding correctness regressions and providing safe rollback. This is explicitly a working doc: sketches, tradeoffs, and next steps.

Context / motivation

- We have a backlog of models and kernel variants where early emission can cut p99 latency by ~5–20% depending on sequence distribution.
- Risk: incorrect token outputs when KV state is stale or kernel selection misfires.
- Need a coordinator that: can opt a model into early emission, monitor divergence, and quickly rollback to conservative path.

What "Early Emission" means here

- A worker may start emitting candidate tokens (and stream partial responses) using a fast-path kernel and a locally extrapolated KV prefix while a full KV fetch or kernel verification is in-flight.
- If downstream validation (acceptance criteria) fails, we must either (a) retract emit (best-effort) and re-emit corrected tokens, or (b) stream correction messages and mark output as possibly inconsistent.

Scope and non-goals

- Scope: coordinator behavior, admission & rollback policy, metrics to drive decisions, and integration notes for model onboarding.
- Non-goal: changing model weights or training. Also does not cover client API change — streaming semantics are presumed backwards-compatible.

Coordinator design sketch

1) Admission state machine (per model-version):
   - OFF: no early emission allowed.
   - MONITOR: early emission allowed on a small canary fraction (e.g., 1% of requests) with extra validation hooks.
   - STAGED: higher fraction (10–30%), still gated by validation windows.
   - ENABLED: full traffic default for that tier/model if metric thresholds met.

   Transitions are time + metric driven. Manual override available (console + API).

2) Per-request flow (worker view):
   - Step 0: routing policy picks model-variant and kernel candidate list.
   - Step 1: if model admission != OFF and random-sample passes, mark request as EE (early-emission).
   - Step 2: quick local KV probe (best-effort partial fetch) + fast kernel selection. If probe indicates possible staleness (TTL mismatch, checksum diff), worker MAY still early-emit but tag emission as "provisional".
   - Step 3: start full KV fetch / canonical kernel activation in parallel.
   - Step 4: if canonical path confirms provisional tokens -> mark accepted; else trigger rollback path (see below).

3) Rollback / correction paths (in order of preference):
   - Silent replay: when canonical path completes, if tokens differ, worker silently replays corrected tokens to the response stream with a "correction" envelope.
   - Rewind+replace: if the client supports rewind+replace RPC, issue replace sequence (preferred for deterministic clients).
   - Fallback annotation: if neither is possible, mark response metadata with "consistency_warning" and send corrected trailing tokens as separate message.

Acceptance criteria & safety contracts (model onboarding)

- Before moving from MONITOR -> STAGED, model must pass the following for a defined evaluation window (>= 24h):
  * Accuracy divergence: token-level edit distance vs canonical path under sampled traffic <= 0.6% at p99 (configurable per-model).
  * Semantic regressions: a small eval suite of prompts (curated by model owner) must show no-severity regressions (semantic change that changes factual assertions) > 0.2% over baseline.
  * Latency benefit: p95 reduction >= 6% vs canonical path for sampled request mix.
  * Stability: rate of rollback-triggering events <= 0.1% of EE requests.

- Metrics must be emitted by default: early_emit_attempts, early_emit_accepted, early_emit_rejected, rollback_count, correction_latency_ms, streamed_correction_rate, consistency_warnings_emitted.

Rollback mechanics and operational playbook

- Immediate rollback: If rollback_count for a model crosses threshold (e.g., 0.3% within 1h at STAGED), auto-transition to MONITOR and notify on-call.
- Kill-switch: global switch to turn EE OFF across tenants (SRE). Console action should propagate within 30s via control-plane pub/sub.
- Incident response runbook (short):
  1) SRE page is created with model id and commit hash.
  2) Set admission -> MONITOR for model, disable STAGED/ENABLED.
  3) Increase sampling of canonical-only routing for affected model to collect more traces.
  4) If root cause is kernel bug, revert kernel PR or force kernel variant until fix.

Metrics & instrumentation (detail)

Key metric definitions (names used in telemetry):
- ee.request.sampled: count of requests selected for EE.
- ee.emit.provisional: provisional early emit attempts.
- ee.emit.accepted: number of provisional emits that matched canonical tokens.
- ee.emit.different: provisional emits that diverged (token edit distance > threshold).
- ee.rollback.trigger: times canonical path caused correction.
- ee.correction.latency_ms: time between provisional emit and final correction available.
- ee.client-corrected: count of client-visible correction messages.
- ee.traffic_fraction: proportion of traffic on EE for model-version.

SLO-like alarms to create:
- If ee.emit.different / ee.request.sampled > X (X default 0.5%) => alert + auto-demote.
- If ee.correction.latency_ms.p99 > 500ms => page (user visible churn).
- If ee.rollback.trigger_rate > 1/min for a model => investigate.

Operational telemetry requirements

- Trace context must link provisional emission to canonical verification run (trace id + subspan id).
- Store sample of provisional vs canonical token sequences (hashed) for at least 7 days for diffs. Hash to protect PII.
- Dashboard per-model showing traffic fraction, divergence rate, p95/p99 latency delta, and recent rollbacks.

Kernel selection signals & constraints

- Fast path kernels should be chosen based on: current sequence length, model's kv-coherence history, and recent divergence rate.
- Kernel metadata to propagate with request: kernel-id, quantization-profile, expected-kv-version, allowed-emit-mode (strict/provisional).
- Kernel-level contract: kernel must provide a quick-check API that returns (likely_coherent:bool, confidence_score:0..1, probe_cost_ms:int). Coordinator uses this to pick whether to early-emit.

KV cache semantics and snapshotting

- Workers maintain per-model-version kv-watermark (last-known canonical epoch). Early emission relies on a fast local prefix snapshot derived from in-memory cache + best-effort fetch.
- Define "snapshot freshness" score: TTL remaining, checksum match to control-plane epoch, missing-keys-percent. Use a simple scoring function to decide provisional vs strict emits.

- When canonical fetch finishes and mismatch found: if mismatch pertains only to trailing KV keys (not prefix used to generate already-emitted tokens) we prefer silent-rewrite; otherwise force a correction flow.

Model onboarding checklist (EE-specific additions)

- Owner provides small eval prompt set (~200 prompts) covering edge cases.
- Define per-model thresholds for token-edit-distance, semantic regression tolerance, and traffic fraction to attempt.
- Implement kernel quick-check API for that model variant.
- Add model to MONITOR for initial 24–72h with 0.5% sampling and automated diff collection.

Testing & validation plan

- Local e2e harness: simulate worker with configurable kv-staleness, run synthetic traffic and assert that acceptance metrics behave. Ticket: INF-4821-test.
- Chaos test: inject KV eviction events during STAGED window and validate rollback throttle.
- Canary rollout: start MONITOR -> STAGED in a single region and validate cross-region divergence separately.

Open questions / tradeoffs

- How expensive is storing diffs? We want 7-day retention at 1% sampling of global traffic; cost needs rough estimate.
- Client UX: do we expose corrected tokens as a stream replacement, or as an appended correction message? Currently prefer minimal API change (append correction + metadata) to avoid client breakage.
- Consistency semantics: is a small token-level divergence acceptable for some models (creative) but not for others (retrieval/factual)? We need per-model classification.
- Can we do probabilistic reconciliation (stop issuing correction if downstream user didn't notice)? Risky for correctness use-cases.

Next steps / action items

- [Maya] Build a minimal coordinator prototype that toggles admission and emits metrics (2w).
- [Sofia] Wire kernel quick-check API surface and sample implementation for quantized kernels (1w).
- [Liam] Add telemetry plumbing: provisional vs canonical trace linking + metric names (1w).
- [Priya] Draft console UI mock for admission transitions and emergency kill-switch (1wk).
- Schedule a 1hr design review with SRE + product-hosted-api to align rollback thresholds.

Notes to self / fragments

- CLI toggles: redwood ctl model set-admission --model-id X --mode MONITOR --frac 0.005
- Slack: #serving-runtime threads for kernel regressions. Seen some p99 noise after q4 kernel PRs — keep an eye.
- TODO: confirm legal/privacy before storing diffs (hashing might be enough, but check with privacy team).

Appendix: example signal calculation (toy)

- snapshot_freshness = 0.7*min(1, ttl_seconds/60) + 0.3*(1 - missing_keys_percent)
- early_emit_allowed = snapshot_freshness > 0.8 AND kernel_confidence > 0.65
- provisional_to_accepted_rate = ee.emit.accepted / ee.emit.provisional (goal > 99.2% in MONITOR)

End of doc.

(rough / iterative — will convert to more formal RFC once prototype data exists)
